nodes.text: insurance and reinsurance companies are required to implement management systems that will assure correct and prudent management of the business in consideration of its nature, scale and complexity.
nodes.mandatory_action: Insurance and reinsurance companies must implement management systems for prudent business management.

nodes.text: Insurance and reinsurance companies are required to maintain written rules of risk management, internal controls, internal audits and outsourcing, to be reviewed annually, mainly in the framework of n
nodes.mandatory_action: Insurance and reinsurance companies must maintain and annually review written rules of risk management, internal controls, internal audits, and outsourcing.

nodes.text: they should be subject to regular internal reviews every year as a minimum
nodes.mandatory_action: Conduct regular internal reviews of the control mechanisms at least annually.

nodes.text: they should be approved by an administrative, management or supervisory authority
nodes.mandatory_action: Obtain approval of the control mechanisms from the relevant authority.

nodes.text: a control system should be verified by a supervisory authority with regard to risks identified by the insurer that may affect adequate financial standing
nodes.mandatory_action: A control system must be verified by a supervisory authority regarding identified risks.

nodes.text: a supervisory authority should have the right to require improvement and strengthening of the management system
nodes.mandatory_action: A supervisory authority must have the right to mandate improvements to the management system.

nodes.text: rules of risk management, internal audit, internal control and outsourcing should be executed in writing
nodes.mandatory_action: Rules of risk management, internal audit, internal control, and outsourcing must be documented in writing.

nodes.text: companies were required to establish audit committees by 6 December, 2009, i.e. within six months of the effective date of the amended Expert Auditors Act.
nodes.mandatory_action: Companies must establish audit committees by the specified deadline.

nodes.text: companies were required to establish by 6 December, 2009, i.e. within six months of the effective date of the amended Expert Auditors Act.
nodes.mandatory_action: Companies must establish an audit committee by December 6, 2009.

nodes.text: Audit committees must have a minimum of three members, including at least one independent member with accounting or financial auditing qualifications.
nodes.mandatory_action: Audit committees must consist of at least three members, including one independent member with relevant qualifications.

nodes.text: audit commissions consisting of a minimum of 3 members, including at least 1 member meeting the conditions of independence with accounting or financial auditing qualifications
nodes.mandatory_action: Audit commissions must consist of a minimum of 3 members, including at least 1 independent member with accounting or financial auditing qualifications.

nodes.text: supervisory boards comprising not more than 5 members
nodes.mandatory_action: Supervisory boards must comprise no more than 5 members.

nodes.text: businesses are obliged to set them up and supply them with relevant instruments and mechanisms of control.
nodes.mandatory_action: Businesses must establish audit committees and provide them with necessary tools and controls.
